## 6. Activity, deterministic scheduling and actual system action

The metric theorem supplies

    error_K<=2aT sqrt(K+1)exp(mu/2)2^(-K/2),
    E exp(theta C)<=exp[Lambda T(exp(theta)-1)],
    Jmax=O(Lambda T+log(1/epsilon)).                     (15)

Take a dyadic maximum duration within a factor two of

    min{kappa/[256a^2(K+1)], T/(p+Jmax+3)}.              (16)

The a=0 branch emits nothing from vacuum and uses ordinary system evolution, so it does not divide by a. The T=0 branch applies the prescribed zero-time instruments. At positive a,T, the deterministic number of first-event calls obeys

    S_calls=O(a^2 K(K+1)pmax T/gamma
                   +Lambda T+p+log(1/epsilon)+1),
    S_calls*tau=O(T).                                  (17)

Furthermore a_P a_inv>=a^2, so the first extensive term is at most a polynomial in K,pmax times Lambda T. This is near-linear **activity**, rather than a surviving aT window penalty. In the rapid limit a proportional to sqrt(gamma), with Lambda fixed, the schedule does not regain a sqrt(rate) loop.

The bridge candidate-immigration mean is at most `G_rate*tau/2=O(1/(K+1))`. The actual acquired scalar source therefore has candidate cap `Hcap=O(log(S_calls/epsilon)+log(K+1)+1)` and virtual word cap `Vcap=O(K+Hcap)`, with no rate-sized loop. Original source tie/boundary cuts now also price the C Gaussian dwell derivative, of norm O(KR), and filter errors. They enlarge bits only logarithmically.

Each free **Gaussian** dwell has actual gate cost O~(M^2 K) plus polynomial one-particle arithmetic. Fixed filters are similarly acquired. For H_S use the actual controlled block encoding of normalization h. The binary-duration circuit for a slot of maximum tau uses fixed durations tau/2^b. The sum of durations of the ACTUAL controlled calls is at most tau per slot. Combining (17) with O(A0 Vcap) slots per first-event call gives

    Q_H=O(A0 Vcap hT
       +S_calls A0 Vcap B[1+log(B/delta_slot)]),
    Q_Q=O(S_calls A0 Vcap),                              (18)

up to actual selected-coupling overhead. This is exactly the legitimate bounded-duration accounting emphasized by N1512; merely summing one realized path's durations would not justify it. Multiply Q_H and Q_Q by the REAL per-query gate costs. Gaussian matrix/rotation work, scalar source arithmetic, CDF preparation, filters, controls and consumer costs are added separately.

# Finite receiving of the new activity compiler

This records the changes needed to the preserved finite-bit proof, rather than treating a source isometry or its normalization as an input. The underlying standard scalar-source, amplification and controlled-duration arguments are credited to the actual N1511/N1512 sources. The new Gaussian/filter/weighted-CDF conjunction remains author-derived.

## Inputs and certificate errors

Use actual finite classical H,E,c_j and actual precision-capable system block circuits. Form A from Hermitian H and the loss factor E so passivity is exact. Check a rational/finite enclosure of P>=I and A^dagger P+PA<=-gamma P with declared slack. Acquire a certified pmax>=||P|| and upper bounds for a,a_P,a_inv. A computed numerical eigenvalue alone is insufficient. The explicit rank-one family has analytic margins; rounding P requires extra logarithmic rate bits because it is multiplied by A. General supplied certificates retain their actual conditioning/slack costs.

Z is bounded between I and (1+1/K)I. Its square roots, inverse square roots, logarithms and approximate diagonalizing unitary are finite M-dimensional calculations. Tiny pivots/eigenvalue degeneracies are handled by absolute approximation, as in the stage-two Gaussian circuit. There is no exponentially large sector diagonalization or inverse small eigenvalue of Z. A certified approximation error O(delta/K) in a one-particle contraction gives O(delta) error in its second quantization. The same bound, with the constant filter norm, prices S/2 and S^(-1).

The contraction drift C has norm at most O(R+gamma), with a uniform dissipativity certificate. Its exponential has the same explicitly paid scaling/squaring and Julia/Givens/binary-Fock implementation as stage two. The actual Gaussian block cost is O~(M^2 K) plus polynomial small-matrix arithmetic. It is called, not assumed, at every virtual dwell and inverse/amplification slot.

## The imported scalar source has matched parameters

Its physical scalar rates are delta=kappa/2 and nu=2g^2/kappa. Endpoints lie in 0..K. The chosen windows make nu*tau=O(1/(K+1)), so its candidate Poisson cap is logarithmic in the final error/call budget.
